subject: MSA & Order Form — liability caps and damage-category carve-outs
messages:
From: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@nova-analytics.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Tara Li <tara.li@nova-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Mar 2027 16:08:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on liability cap + consequential exclusion (MSA/Order Form)

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team was impressed. Procurement and legal at Nova are reviewing the MSA + Order Form and we have a couple of open items that could block signature: primarily the liability cap interplay with the consequential/special damages exclusion.

Two items they asked us to confirm:
- Are the consequential/special/incidental/punitive damage exclusions mutual or one-way (i.e., does Nova expect Redwood to be carved out one-way)?
- Which events are carved out from the cap (e.g., IP indemnity, breach of confidentiality, gross negligence, willful misconduct)?

They sent a mark-up but I want to get your baseline before we escalate to legal-to-legal. Can you send your preferred language or confirm a starting compromise?

Appreciate it — Evan

--
Evan Brooks
Head of Platform Partnerships
Nova Analytics
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@nova-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Mar 2027 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on liability cap + consequential exclusion (MSA/Order Form)

Evan —

Great, thanks for flagging. Short answer up-front: Redwood prefers a mutual exclusion for consequential/special/incidental/punitive damages, with narrow carve-outs to the cap for: IP infringement/indemnity, gross negligence/willful misconduct, and breaches of confidentiality/personal data. That keeps the commercial risk balanced while preserving the practical cap mechanics for both sides.

What we typically propose:
- Consequential damages excluded (mutual) but defined explicitly (lost profits, loss of business, loss of use, etc.).
- Carve-outs from cap include: (a) indemnity for third-party IP claims; (b) unauthorized access to personal data/confidentiality breach; (c) gross negligence/willful misconduct.
- No automatic unlimited liability otherwise — the Order Form should keep the overall cap (e.g., 12 months of fees) but the carve-outs remain.

I'll loop in Marissa to propose redline language that we can swap with Nova legal. If Nova insists on a one-way exclusion, we'll need to understand the commercial driver so we can come back with a concession matrix (e.g., higher cap / shorter SLA credits / additional indemnities).

Next steps: Marissa will attach suggested language; can we schedule a legal-to-legal call tomorrow to walk through the redlines?

Thanks —
Stephanie
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@nova-analytics.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Mar 2027 19:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on liability cap + consequential exclusion (MSA/Order Form)

Evan / Stephanie —

Attaching a clean redline (Nova_Redlines_v3.docx) with two options for Nova legal:

Option A (preferred by Redwood legal) — mutual exclusion + explicit definition:
- "Neither party shall be liable to the other for consequential, incidental, special, exemplary or punitive damages, including but not limited to loss of profits, loss of business, loss of data or loss of use."
- Carve-outs from the cap: (i) indemnity obligations for third-party IP claims; (ii) breach of confidentiality or unauthorized access to Personal Data; (iii) damages resulting from gross negligence or willful misconduct; (iv) claims subject to mandatory statutory liability (where applicable).

Option B (commercial concession) — one-way exclusion in favor of Nova, paired with: higher overall cap (e.g., 24 months fees) + enhanced SLA credits + explicit limits on remedies for data incidents to expedite incident response.

I also added a short definition block (see doc) to avoid debate over what counts as "consequential" — that tends to be where negotiations stall.

If Nova comes back with specific suggested language, please have legal paste it into the doc rather than free-text in the body — it speeds review.

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
Attachment: Nova_Redlines_v3.docx (redline of MSA and Order Form)
From: Tara Li <tara.li@nova-analytics.com>

Date: Tue, 22 Mar 2027 08:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on liability cap + consequential exclusion (MSA/Order Form)

Hi Stephanie,

Appreciate the quick reply and Marissa's options. Wanted to share Nova's position so we're transparent before a legal call:

- Procurement is pushing for one-way language that protects Nova from consequential damages arising from Redwood's service interruption. Their concern is material business interruption tied to a core data pipeline.
- Legal is okay with a mutual exclusion only if the carve-outs from the cap are very clearly enumerated and if Redwood accepts a higher cap (they prefer 2x the proposed cap).

I've attached our latest mark-up (Nova_Response_Redlines.docx). Two asks from our side before legal-to-legal:
1) Can Redwood confirm whether you will accept a mutual exclusion with a 24-month fee cap and the carve-outs Marissa listed?
2) If not, can you provide an alternative commercial concession (pricing credit, extended uptime SLA, or additional indemnities) that would get procurement comfortable with a mutual position?

Thanks — happy to discuss on a quick call.

Best,
Tara Li
Head of Procurement
Nova Analytics

Tara / Evan —

Thanks for the clarity, and for the Nova redline. To keep this moving, here is a concrete compromise we can present to our exec/legal team and to Nova:

Proposed compromise (can be done in the MSA with a short Order Form call-out):
- Consequential/special/incidental/punitive damages: mutual exclusion with a clear definition block (lost profits, loss of business, loss of use, indirect damages).
- Carve-outs from cap (explicitly listed):
  * Third-party IP indemnity;
  * Breach of confidentiality or unauthorized access to Personal Data;
  * Gross negligence or willful misconduct;
  * Fraud or intentional misconduct.
- Overall cap: 24 months of fees (as a commercial concession to Nova) but only for direct damages; carve-outs above are not capped.
- If Nova insists on a one-way exclusion instead of mutual, Redwood can consider that only if Nova agrees to: (a) 36 months fee cap; (b) faster escalations and a 25% credit on first-month fees for first year as a commercial sweetener; and (c) a joint incident review SLA added to the Order Form.

Action items:
- Marissa: finalize redline adopting the agreed compromise and prepare a 1-page summary (MSA-exception-summary.pdf) for exec review.
- Tara / Nova: confirm whether you accept the mutual-exclusion + 24-month cap route or prefer to test the one-way concession.
- Scheduling: Let's do legal-to-legal tomorrow at 11:00 AM PT to resolve wording details. I'll send a calendar invite.

If everyone agrees in principle on the mutual exclusion + 24-month cap, we can fold final language into the Order Form and push DocuSign for signature.

Cheers,
Stephanie
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
